subject: Capacity sweep & soft-pledge: HelixBridge late-stage go-live prep
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Capacity sweep & soft-pledge: HelixBridge late-stage go-live prep

Team —

HelixBridge (deal HB-4721) is moving to final contract review and their target pilot start is 2029-06-10. Sales says this is effectively a hard deadline for the first tranche of nodes (see deal notes link below). Before we sign, Legal and Sales are asking operations to confirm end-to-end availability and to place a brief soft-pledge on capacity so we aren't overtaken by last-minute spikes.

Request: can infra run a quick availability sweep and confirm the following by EOD Monday, 2029-05-13 PST:  
- Thermal-binned node counts for NVID-4 and NVID-8 class (target: 8x NVID-8, 24x NVID-4 for initial 3-month pilot)
- Expected token-throughput headroom at 8k context with current kernel set (no additional quantization)
- Any infra-level blockers for a 72-hour soft-hold starting 2029-05-20 (we'd like ops to mark a provisional hold that can be released/converted after contract signature)

I attached the customer requirements sheet (helix_requirements_20290510.xlsx) and a quick CSV with last-week utilization. Please include any recommended fallbacks (e.g., model variant downgrade, reduced batch size) and an ops playbook snippet for a rollback if we need to decommit.

Why now: sales is asking for explicit operational confirmation to avoid a post-signing scramble. We should err on caution and hold minimal runway rather than promise and fail.

Thanks — I.

--
Irene Choi
Manager, Deal Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity sweep & soft-pledge: HelixBridge late-stage go-live prep

Irene — thanks for the heads up and the sheet. Quick summary after an initial pass:

- Inventory: we currently have 12 NVID-8 class slots and ~40 NVID-4 class slots across us-west-2 pools; 2 NVID-8s are already earmarked for other late-stage opportunities through May.
- Thermal bins: after accounting for existing reservations and expected maintenance windows, realistic available numbers for the requested window (2029-05-20 to 2029-05-23) are ~6 NVID-8 and ~28 NVID-4. We can provision an additional +2 NVID-8 by pulling from a low-utilization cluster if we accept a 24h staging/validation window.
- Throughput: with the current kernel selection (AVX fused attention v3), and no extra quantization, we estimate sustained throughput of ~320 tokens/sec per NVID-8 at 8k context for the incumbent model family. That maps to the requested QPS if their peak concurrency remains <= 12.

Open questions for sales:
1) Is HelixBridge planning to use full FP16 weights or accept q4_0/q4_k8 variants for the pilot? If they accept a quantized variant we can increase practical headroom by ~30% (fewer hotspots).
2) Do they require dedicated pool/tenant isolation from day one or are shared pools acceptable for pilot?

Operational ask: we can apply a 72-hour soft-pledge (internal tag + capacity remark in the booking system) for the window starting 2029-05-20 but I need confirmation on the quantization plan and whether we should stage the two additional NVID-8s (adds a 24h validation window).

I'll attach the short ops snapshot and a one-pager on the validation steps.

-rishi

Attachment: capacity_snapshot_20290510.csv
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 10 May 2029 12:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity sweep & soft-pledge: HelixBridge late-stage go-live prep

Thanks both — quick answers to Rishi's Qs from GTM:  

1) HelixBridge is open to starting on q4_0 for the pilot. Their engineering lead (Alex) said they will accept a quantized variant for the first 8 weeks to accelerate time-to-live. We will put the full FP16 rollout on the roadmap for month-3.
2) Pilot isolation: they asked for logical isolation (dedicated namespace, token-level logging) but not physical dedicated nodes for the pilot. They want the option to move to a dedicated pool in the Q2 renewal.

Committed numbers (from the momentum call): initial pilot needs 8 NVID-8-equivalent throughput points and capacity for steady-state 12 concurrent inference streams. If we quantize as above, Rishi's estimates look conservative and workable.

Action: please apply the 72-hour soft-pledge starting 2029-05-20 and stage +2 NVID-8s for 24h validation (we'll confirm after legal closes). I'll loop Sam and Alex once we have the ops note and the pledge recorded.

Marcus
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: Sam Taylor <sam.taylor@helixbridge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Chen <alex.chen@helixbridge.ai>
Date: Mon, 13 May 2029 16:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Capacity sweep & soft-pledge: HelixBridge late-stage go-live prep

Marcus / Irene — appreciate the fast turnaround and the clear operational plan. We can confirm:
- q4_0 variant for pilot is acceptable.
- logical isolation is fine for the initial tranche.
- target pilot start remains 2029-06-10; if you can mark the 72-hour soft-pledge window starting 2029-05-20 that will be very helpful for our internal signoff.

Please let us know if you need any further detail from our SRE team — Alex is copied.

Thanks,
Sam
Head of Platform
HelixBridge
